bib.title: wav2vec 2.0: A Framework for Self-Supervised Learning of Speech Representations

question: Can representations learned from unlabeled speech audio alone, then fine-tuned on little transcribed data, match or beat semi-supervised ASR?
hypothesis: If a pre-trained model captures the structure of speech, it should need few labeled examples to fine-tune for speech recognition.
contributions: Framework masking latent speech representations with a jointly learned quantizer and contrastive task
State of the art on TIMIT and Librispeech 100h clean; 1.8/3.3 WER on full Librispeech
Ultra-low resource ASR with 10 minutes of labels

method.summary: CNN feature encoder maps raw audio to latents; spans are masked and a Transformer builds contexts; a contrastive loss identifies the true Gumbel-softmax product-quantized latent among 100 distractors, plus a diversity loss. The model is then fine-tuned with CTC on labeled data.
method.task: self-supervised speech pretraining, then CTC ASR and TIMIT phoneme recognition

models.name: wav2vec 2.0 BASE
models.architecture: 7-block conv feature encoder (512 ch, strides 5,2,2,2,2,2,2, kernels 10,3,3,3,3,2,2) + Transformer, conv relative position (kernel 128, 16 groups), product quantizer

other.encoder_output: 49 Hz, 20 ms stride, 25 ms receptive field

models.name: Transformer LM (decoding)
models.architecture: 20 blocks, dim 1280, FFN 6144, 16 heads, identical to [51]

training.objective: L = Lm + alpha*Ld; contrastive loss over K=100 distractors (kappa=0.1) plus codebook diversity loss; fine-tune with CTC
training.lr: pretrain peak 5e-4 BASE, 3e-4 LARGE; fine-tune 2e-5 or 3e-5 (1e-4 BASE 960h)
training.lr_schedule: pretrain: warmup then linear decay; fine-tune: tri-state (10% warmup, 40% constant, linear decay)
training.warmup: pretrain first 8% of updates; fine-tune first 10%
training.batch_size: pretrain BASE 1.6h total (1.4m samples/GPU), LARGE 2.7h (1.2m samples/GPU); fine-tune BASE 1600 sec, LARGE 1920 sec
training.steps: pretrain 400k BASE, 250k LARGE, 600k LARGE LV-60k; fine-tune 12k/13k/20k/50k/320k (10min/1h/10h/100h/960h), TIMIT 40k
training.dropout: 0.1 in Transformer, feature encoder output and quantizer input; LayerDrop 0.05 BASE, 0.2 LARGE pretrain (none on LV-60k); fine-tune LayerDrop 0.05 BASE, 0.1 LARGE
training.regularisation: fine-tune SpecAugment-like masking (span 10 time steps, 64-channel spans); Librispeech pretraining: L2 on last encoder layer activations, encoder gradient scaled by 0.1
training.hardware: 64 V100 BASE; 128 V100 LARGE; fine-tune 8 GPUs BASE, 24 GPUs LARGE
training.wall_clock: BASE 1.6 days; LARGE 2.3 days LS-960, 5.2 days LV-60k

other.masking: p=0.065, M=10, ~49% masked, mean span 14.7 (299 ms)
other.gumbel_tau: 2 annealed to min 0.5 BASE / 0.1 LARGE, factor 0.999995 per update
other.finetune_first_10k_updates: only output classifier trained; feature encoder frozen
other.ablation_setup: BASE LS-960 250k updates, p=0.075, fine-tune train-10h 60k updates 1 GPU 640k samples/batch

inference.samples: deterministic decode; 3 fine-tuning seeds in ablations

parameters.LM weight search: Bayesian optimization (Ax), 128 trials, LM weight in [0,5], word insertion in [-5,5], tuned on dev-other

metrics.name: WER
metrics.definition: word error rate on Librispeech dev/test clean/other

metrics.name: PER
metrics.definition: phoneme error rate on TIMIT, 39 classes

eval.protocol: Libri-light protocol for low-resource splits; ablations average 3 fine-tuning seeds on combined dev-clean/other

evidence.quote: we sample p = 0.065 of all time-steps to be starting indices and mask the subsequent M = 10 time-steps

results.table: Table 9, row 10 min LARGE LV-60k None, columns test clean/other (40.2, 38.7)

results.quote: it still achieves WER 3.2/6.1, an error reduction of 24%/29% relative to iterative self-training.

results.claim: Quantizing only the targets (continuous inputs) is best: dev avg WER 7.97, vs 12.18 when both quantized.

results.table: Table 4, row Baseline, column avg. WER (7.97); Quantized inputs, quantized targets 12.18

results.note: Table 4: continuous inputs continuous targets 8.58; quantized inputs continuous targets 11.18.
results.quote: The training accuracy of identifying the correct latent audio representation increases from 62% to 78.0% when switching from quantized to continuous targets.

results.claim: Supervised from-scratch LARGE with the same architecture gets 2.1/4.6 on 960h, vs pretrained 1.8/3.3.
results.quote: supervised training of our architecture achieves WER 2.1/4.6 (LARGE - from scratch)

results.claim: Full 960h: semi-supervised noisy student (LSTM LM) still scores 1.7/3.4, better than wav2vec 2.0 on test-clean.
results.table: Table 2, row Noisy student [42], columns test clean/other (1.7, 3.4)

results.table: Table 9, 10 min LARGE LV-60k 4-gram test other 10.3; Transf. 8.2

results.claim: Joint learning of discrete units cuts WER by about a third vs discrete BERT with separate quantization.
results.quote: reducing WER by a about a third.

limits: Uses character CTC with a word-level LM, which the authors say delays LM feedback; they expect gains from seq2seq and word pieces
Not combined with self-training; authors say the two are likely complementary
Ablations use a reduced setup (BASE, 250k updates, train-10h)
English only (Librispeech/LibriVox, TIMIT); multilingual claim is hope in Broader Impact
Section 5.1 text gives 5.2/8.6 for the 10 min LARGE LV-60k model while Table 1 gives 4.8/8.2
Ablation text says p=0.065 baseline in Table 5 label p=0.075; Sec 4.2 main models use p=0.065

lineage.note: two-step quantize then contextualize; wav2vec 2.0 cuts WER by about a third
quantization and product quantizer design; here learned end-to-end

lineage.work: Improved noisy student training for ASR

figures.caption: Illustration of our framework which jointly learns contextualized speech representations and an inventory of discretized speech units.
figures.why: shows CNN, masking, Transformer and quantized targets in one picture

figures.caption: Average WER and standard deviation on combined dev-clean/other of Librispeech for three training seeds. We ablate quantizing the context network input and the targets in the contrastive loss.
figures.why: core design choice: quantize targets only
